title: VF-MT303-VmLifecycleStateMachine
clause: Hand-rolled VmLifecycle enum + pure step(observed, desired) -> Plan of ordered idempotent check-then-act steps, EventLedger intent journaling before every side effect, observed liveness = process alive AND heartbeat fresh, generation fencing on all writes

scope.summary:
GOAL: Implement the brain of the fleet reconciler as a pure, hand-rolled state machine: enum VmLifecycle + fn step(observed, desired) -> Plan, plugged into MT-302's FleetReconcileStep seam. The design is the research catalog's P20 (hand-rolled enums, transitions persisted; the enum lives in Rust, the CURRENT STATE lives in SurrealDB - no state-machine framework crate) combined with P10's flintlock plan/step reconciliation (a Plan is an ordered list of idempotent check-then-act steps executed against the host) and P2's check-every-property idempotency (assume the previous pass crashed at any point; every property independently checked and repaired). The state machine's most important single rule comes from flintlock issue #326 (P10 avoid-clause): a VM is NEVER considered alive because a spawn call returned Ok - flintlock marked VMs CREATED when 'the call to FC api succeeds' while the process 'started and died and we dont check'. Observed liveness here is process alive (adapter status reports Running - CloudHypervisorAdapter::status, adapter.rs line 2398) AND heartbeat fresh (heartbeat_at_utc within threshold, model_lane.rs line 6571); spawn-Ok yields VmLifecycle::Pending until the first fresh heartbeat is observed.

STATES (hand-rolled, serde snake_case, persisted as TEXT with CHECK constraint added in MT-304's migration touch or a dedicated column note - the ENUM lives in Rust, per P20):
   pub enum VmLifecycle { Pending, Restoring, RestoredPaused, Running, PausedForSnapshot, Quarantined, TearingDown, Gone }
   RestoredPaused and PausedForSnapshot are first-class states because Cloud Hypervisor's snapshot/restore discipline (P13) has explicit paused intermediate states: restore produces a VM 'restored in a paused state' requiring explicit resume, and snapshot requires pause first - a crash mid-snapshot must leave an unambiguous resumable state, never an implicit limbo. These states double as the VMM-binary live-upgrade path (snapshot on old binary, restore on new).

PURE PLANNER (research P20, P21 foundation):
   pub struct ObservedVmState { pub lifecycle: VmLifecycle, pub binding: Option<WorktreeVmBindingRecord>, pub process_running: bool, pub heartbeat_fresh: bool, pub binding_generation: i64, pub desired_generation: i64 }
   pub struct FleetPlan { pub steps: Vec<PlanStep>, pub fenced_generation: i64 }
   pub enum PlanStep { EnsureVmSpawned, VerifyFirstHeartbeat, ResumeRestoredVm, PauseForSnapshot, CaptureSnapshot, ResumeAfterSnapshot, KillVm, ReleaseWorkspaceResources, MarkGone, NoOp }
   pub fn step(observed: &ObservedVmState, desired: &FleetDesiredStateRecord) -> FleetPlan
   step() is a PURE function: no IO, no clock reads (freshness is computed by the caller and passed in), no randomness - this purity is what makes MT-307's proptest-state-machine harness sufficient without a simulation runtime (P21). Every (observed, desired) pair maps deterministically to a plan; unknown/contradictory combinations map to a typed PlannerContradiction outcome, never a panic.

PLAN EXECUTION (research P10, P2, P19):
   Each PlanStep executes as check-then-act: re-verify the precondition immediately before acting (e.g. EnsureVmSpawned first checks whether a live binding already exists via WorktreeVmRegistry - its ensure path is already idempotent and TOCTOU-guarded, worktree_vm_registry.rs ensure_worktree_vm_with_spec_outcome lines 279-418) so a crashed plan reruns from the top safely. Steps execute strictly in order; the first failed step aborts the remainder of the plan (the next level-triggered pass replans from fresh state).
   INTENT JOURNALING (P19): before EVERY side-effectful step, append a typed EventLedger intent record FLEET_INTENT_{STEP} carrying { worktree_id, step, fenced_generation, plan_id } - so a crash or cancellation mid-operation is repairable by the next pass reading the journal tail. Side effect first, journal second is FORBIDDEN.
   GENERATION FENCING: every durable write carries the fenced generation captured at plan time; writes go through UPDATE ... WHERE generation = $fenced (the exact shape of record_snapshot_in_transaction / mark_terminated_in_transaction, worktree_vm_registry.rs lines 1104-1162, whose rows_affected()==0 becomes a typed StaleBinding error) and the desired_generation equivalent from MT-301. A stale plan (superseded intent or superseded binding) MUST fail closed with zero rows affected, never last-writer-wins.

VM OPERATIONS: all through the existing seams only - WorktreeVmRegistry (ensure/snapshot/restore/teardown, worktree_vm_registry.rs lines 254-282, 424-471, 478-487, 720-732) which internally drives CloudHypervisorAdapter (spawn line 2000, spawn_persistent 1764, kill 2314, reclaim_detached 2381, status 2398, snapshot 2444, delete_snapshot 2623, restore 2649). This MT adds NO direct adapter calls and NO adapter modifications; plan steps compose registry calls. Production wiring reuses the factory path (production_factory.rs with_durable_worktree_vm_store 1190-1196 and worktree_vm_registry_for 1217-1244).

RESOURCE PRIVACY: plans operate strictly inside the reconciler's ResourceAccessContext; every registry/store call is already scope-checked (resource_scope.rs ResourceScope 147-153; worktree_vm_registry.rs require_scope 1004-1019). The planner itself never sees rows from another account because MT-301/MT-302 reads are scope-filtered; an assert in the step executor verifies the claim transaction's row scope matches the daemon scope before any side effect.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: new files vm_fleet/lifecycle.rs (enum, ObservedVmState, planner) and vm_fleet/executor.rs (RealReconcileStep implementing MT-302's FleetReconcileStep: fresh-read, compute freshness, plan, journal, execute); mod.rs registration; tests. No migrations in this MT (observed lifecycle is derived, not stored; persisted columns arrive with MT-304/MT-305 where they are needed).

DETAILED SPEC (planner truth table, normative rows - full table in tests):
   (Gone/None observed, desired=running) -> [EnsureVmSpawned, VerifyFirstHeartbeat]
   (Pending, process_running=true, heartbeat_fresh=false) -> [VerifyFirstHeartbeat]  // waiting, not Running yet (flintlock #326)
   (Pending, process_running=false) -> [KillVm, MarkGone] then replan  // spawn-succeeded-then-died: clean up the corpse binding via teardown, next pass respawns
   (Running, desired=snapshotted) -> [PauseForSnapshot, CaptureSnapshot, ResumeAfterSnapshot]  // resume-after because desired snapshotted means checkpoint-and-continue is false: see note; if desired means parked-snapshotted, plan is [PauseForSnapshot, CaptureSnapshot, KillVm, MarkGone-with-snapshot-retained]; the DETAILED decision: desired=snapshotted means PARKED - snapshot captured, VM down, binding_state 'snapshotted' (worktree_vm_registry.rs WorktreeVmBindingState::Snapshotted line 110 is live-adoptable per is_live 137-139)
   (RestoredPaused, desired=running) -> [ResumeRestoredVm, VerifyFirstHeartbeat]
   (PausedForSnapshot observed after crash, desired=running) -> [ResumeAfterSnapshot] if snapshot journal intent shows capture completed, else [CaptureSnapshot, ResumeAfterSnapshot]
   (any live, desired=absent) -> [KillVm, ReleaseWorkspaceResources, MarkGone]  // MarkGone hands off to MT-305 tombstone finalizer once it lands; until then MarkGone maps to registry teardown (mark_terminated_in_transaction shape)
   (Quarantined, any desired) -> [NoOp]  // MT-304 owns quarantine entry/exit; the planner never exits quarantine on its own
   Contradictions (e.g. binding says terminated but process_running=true) -> PlannerContradiction typed outcome; executor journals FLEET_CONTRADICTION and leaves state for the next pass + diagnostics.

STEP-BY-STEP:
1. Read worktree_vm_registry.rs in full (all 1919 lines; the compensation and reconcile paths at 584-933 matter for KillVm/MarkGone step composition), adapter.rs signatures listed above, MT-301 store, MT-302 seam.
2. Implement VmLifecycle + ObservedVmState + FleetPlan + PlanStep + pure step() with the truth table; document every row with a comment citing its research pattern.
3. Implement the observation assembler: durable_binding read + adapter status via registry + heartbeat freshness computed from heartbeat_at_utc against a threshold passed in (no clock reads inside the planner).
4. Implement executor: journal intent -> execute step -> record outcome, generation-fenced writes, first-failure aborts plan.
5. Wire RealReconcileStep into MT-302's dispatcher behind a constructor flag so NoopReconcileStep remains for chassis tests.
6. Tests: pure-planner unit tests over the full truth table (no SurrealDB needed); live-SurrealDB + fake-adapter integration tests for journaling order (intent row exists before the fake adapter records the side effect), generation fencing (stale plan writes zero rows), spawn-then-die remediation, paused-state crash resume, contradiction handling. Spec-Realism Gate: the journaling and fencing tests run against real SurrealDB; the adapter may be the existing fake/trait-mock (real CH execution is proven at the WP integration level).
7. Run proof targets; record measured output. Implementer never marks COMPLETED.

acceptance_criteria: AC-303-1: VmLifecycle { Pending, Restoring, RestoredPaused, Running, PausedForSnapshot, Quarantined, TearingDown, Gone } exists hand-rolled (no state-machine framework crate), serde snake_case, with typed parse errors.

AC-303-2: step(observed, desired) is pure - no IO, no clock, no randomness (code review + grep for Instant/SystemTime/rand in lifecycle.rs) - and total: every input maps to a FleetPlan or a typed PlannerContradiction, never a panic.
AC-303-3: Plans are ordered idempotent check-then-act steps; a live test proves rerunning a partially executed plan from the top is safe (no double spawn, no double snapshot).

AC-303-4: A typed EventLedger intent record is appended BEFORE every side-effectful step; a live test proves the intent row is durable before the fake adapter observes the corresponding call, and grep proof shows no side-effect call precedes its journal call in executor.rs.

AC-303-5: spawn-Ok produces Pending, not Running; only process-running AND heartbeat-fresh observation promotes to Running; the spawn-succeeds-then-process-dies scenario (flintlock #326) is a named test that converges to cleanup + respawn.
AC-303-6: All durable writes are generation-fenced (binding generation and desired_generation); a live test proves a stale-generation plan affects zero rows and surfaces a typed stale error.
AC-303-7: RestoredPaused and PausedForSnapshot are first-class states; a crash injected between pause and snapshot, and between snapshot and resume, each converge on the next pass without data loss.
AC-303-8: The planner emits NoOp for Quarantined states and never exits quarantine (MT-304 owns that); proven by unit test.
AC-303-9: No direct CloudHypervisorAdapter calls in vm_fleet/ (grep proof: adapter access only through WorktreeVmRegistry seams).
AC-303-10: Every truth-table row carries a code comment citing its research pattern (P2/P10/P13/P19/P20 or flintlock #326).

implementation_notes: IMPLEMENTATION GATE: gated on WP-1 IV verdicts + merge to main (expansion_provenance.implementation_gate); MT-302 must land first.

desired=snapshotted means PARKED (snapshot captured, VM down, binding 'snapshotted'): this is the deliberate reading that makes Snapshotted a resource-saving desired state; a live-checkpoint-and-continue desired state is out of scope for this family and must not be improvised.
The planner never reads the clock: heartbeat freshness is computed by the executor and passed in ObservedVmState, preserving purity for MT-307's property harness (P21).

KillVm composition must handle the detached case: registry teardown already distinguishes running vs detached handles (reclaim_detached path, worktree_vm_registry.rs 822-842 and 869-901); do not reimplement that logic.
EventLedger intent records are repair inputs, not an execution queue: the next pass replans from observed state and uses the journal tail only to disambiguate paused-state crashes (P13/P19).
All Rust; SurrealDB/EventLedger authority only; no SQLite; no K8s/Docker/containerd/Nomad; no new external daemons; disk-agnostic paths; no names with spaces.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Pure logic + executor MT; lifecycle transitions become operator-visible through MT-306's FR events and fleet panel. Intent journal records are the projection seam.

target_entries: Workspace fleet > VM lifecycle states (all eight states, what each means, which are crash-resumable)
Workspace fleet > Why a freshly spawned workspace shows Pending until its first heartbeat

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.note: Lifecycle transitions are ledger intent/outcome records in this MT; FR transition events land in MT-306. Record DEFERRED-to-MT-306.
PlannerContradiction outcomes MUST emit a diagnostic event (FLEET_CONTRADICTION) - a contradiction is exactly the state a no-context model needs surfaced to isolate failures without guessing.
The planner is pure and the executor runs inside the MT-302 daemon whose liveness posture is recorded there; no separate long-lived process exists.

risk_if_missed: The reconciler chassis converges nothing: without a correct planner the fleet either copies flintlock's verified failure mode (spawn-Ok treated as alive, dead VMs marked healthy) or improvises non-idempotent workflows that double-spawn VMs and lose paused snapshots on crash.

risks: RISK-1: Spawn-Ok is treated as alive (flintlock #326): a VM that started and immediately died is recorded Running and the workspace silently serves nothing.
RISK-2: A crash between pause and snapshot (or snapshot and resume) leaves a VM paused forever with no state that says why.
RISK-3: Side effect executes before its intent journal lands, so a crash leaves an unattributable half-applied mutation the next pass cannot classify.
RISK-4: Unfenced writes let a stale plan (built against superseded desired or binding generation) overwrite a newer binding - the ABA the registry's StaleBinding machinery exists to prevent.
RISK-5: The planner grows hidden IO or clock reads, silently breaking MT-307's property-testing premise.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): Pending-until-first-heartbeat rule + named spawn-then-die regression test (AC-303-5).
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): RestoredPaused/PausedForSnapshot as first-class states + crash-injection convergence tests (AC-303-7).
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): Journal-before-side-effect ordering proven by live test and grep (AC-303-4).
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): Generation-fenced UPDATE ... WHERE generation = $fenced with zero-rows => typed stale error (AC-303-6), mirroring worktree_vm_registry.rs 1104-1162.
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): Purity grep proof + code review (AC-303-2).
